about.title: About MemorySmith.app
about.heading: Welcome to MemorySmith.app
about.lead: Structured knowledge, natively readable and writable by humans and agents.

what.heading: What this is
what.body: MemorySmith is where you and your AI agents build knowledge together. A notebook holds folders, a folder holds notes in Markdown, and the same notes are read and written from both sides: by you, in this interface, and by an agent, through the connector. Nothing is locked in here: every note stays plain text and keeps its whole history, and every notebook can be exported in full at any time.
what.guidance: What makes a notebook here different is that it says how it wants to be written. Its Guidance states what the notebook is for and how to write in it; each folder carries a description and a Template. An agent reads both before writing a single line, which is how a notebook stays coherent after a hundred notes instead of drifting into a folder of loose files.

interface.heading: What you will find here
interface.body: This interface is a reading tool before it is an editing one. These are the surfaces it gives you:

notebooks.definition: The first screen lists them, with how many notes each one holds and when it last changed. Opening one takes you back to where you stopped reading.

folders.definition: The side panel is the structure of the notebook, in the order the notebook itself declares. A note shows its properties and its text, and each link takes you to the note it reaches — or says it reaches none yet.

guidance.definition: Readable on their own screens, so you can see the rules an agent is following before you read what it wrote.

graph.definition: Every note as a point and every link as a line, which is where an isolated note, or a cluster nobody connected, becomes visible.

search.definition: Across the notes of a notebook, by what they say and by the properties they declare.

transfers.definition: Exporting a notebook, or importing one, from the icon beside your picture. What comes out is a .notebook file holding the notebook — the notes in Markdown, the folders, the Guidance and the Templates, and the history and the files when you choose them — and that file is what an import reads.

connector.heading: Connecting your AI assistant
connector.body: This is the part worth doing today. MemorySmith answers AI tools through a remote MCP server, so an assistant does not merely read your notebooks: it writes in them, obeying the Guidance of the notebook and the Template of each folder. The address of this environment is:

claude.heading: In Claude
claude.one: In the side menu, open Customize and then Connectors.
claude.three: Under Name, write MemorySmith.app; under Remote MCP server URL, paste the address above; click Continue.
claude.four: Claude opens the MemorySmith sign-in page (if it does not, click Connect on the connector); sign in with this same account and authorise it.
claude.five: In a conversation, check under + and then Connectors that MemorySmith.app is switched on, and ask for your notebooks.

chatgpt.heading: In ChatGPT
chatgpt.one: In the browser, not the phone or tablet app, which does not show these options: in Settings, open Plugins, then Developer mode, and switch it on: it is what lets you add a server that is not in the catalogue.
chatgpt.two: In the side menu, open Plugins and click the + beside the search.
chatgpt.three: Under Name, write MemorySmith.app; under Connection, keep Server URL and paste the address above; keep Authentication on OAuth.
chatgpt.four: Tick I understand and want to continue and click Create; the warning is the same for any server outside the catalogue. Sign in with this same account and authorise it.
chatgpt.five: In a conversation, click the +, type MemorySmith, pick the plugin and ask for your notebooks.

connector.sameAccount: Whichever tool you use, sign in with the same account you are reading this with: the assistant reaches exactly the notebooks you reach, with exactly your permissions, and every change it makes is recorded under your name.

agent.heading: What to ask it first
agent.body: You do not have to build anything here by hand. Ask the assistant, in your own words:
agent.one: “Create a notebook in MemorySmith for my reading notes, with the folders that make sense, and write its Guidance.”
agent.two: “Read my notebook and tell me what is missing from it.”
agent.three: “Write a note about what we just discussed, in the right folder.”
agent.skills: The connector carries written methods for the tasks that go wrong most often — designing a notebook from scratch, writing a note this product can read — and a good assistant reads them before it starts. You will see it do so.
